title: Private release train notes (Q2 2025) — cutting process, version mapping, gating proposal
content:
Owner: Connor O’Brien (Release Eng)
Last pass: 2025-06-18
Audience: Release Eng + SRE + Private Deployments engineering

Why this doc exists (context)
- We’re expanding Redwood Private (VPC + on-prem/air-gapped) with a safer upgrade/rollback workflow.
- Release train needs to explicitly tie “platform version” (control plane + data plane charts) to upgrade tooling (installer, terraform module vars, offline bundles) and to a gating policy.
- These notes capture current practice + a proposal for Q2’25 so we stop doing bespoke “one-off” private release cuts.

Terminology (keep consistent)
- Platform version: Redwood Private application stack version shipped via Helm charts (control plane + data plane).
- Installer version: redwood-private-installer CLI that generates plans, runs prechecks, orchestrates backup/restore hooks, and invokes helm/terraform.
- Terraform module version: redwood-terraform module release that wires version pinning + artifact sources + upgrade window.
- Bundle version: air-gapped “upgrade bundle” containing charts/images + checksums/signatures + manifest.

Current state (as of early Q2)
- Private releases are cut “when ready” with a heavy manual checklist.
- Version skew is common:
  - Customers run platform vX while using older installer that doesn’t know about new prechecks/rollback entry points.
  - On-prem customers can’t reliably verify offline bundles; failures become support tickets.
- Most gating is “social”: Release Eng asks SRE/Platform to eyeball test results and say yes.

Goal state for Q2
- A repeatable Private release train with:
  - deterministic version mapping rules
  - minimum test matrix and gates
  - evidence attached to every cut (what passed, what was waived, who approved)
- Default supported upgrade path: N-1 -> N (no multi-hop automation requirement in first GA of upgrade/rollback mechanism).


Release train cadence proposal (Q2)
- Weekly “candidate cut” (RC) if the required gates are green; otherwise skip.
- Monthly “stable” Private release (customer-facing recommendation) from the best RC.
- Emergency patch releases allowed anytime, but must satisfy minimum safety bar (see “Emergency lane”).

Suggested calendar (example)
- Tue: Branch cut for Private RC (charts + platform gating config)
- Wed: Nightly integration matrix completes (VPC + on-prem, N-1 -> N upgrade)
- Thu: SRE + Release Eng review gate + approval
- Fri: Publish artifacts (hosted artifact repo + offline bundle) + internal comms to Solutions/Support


What exactly is “a Private release” (artifact checklist)
A Private release is considered shippable only when ALL of the following are versioned and published:
1) Helm charts
   - redwood-control-plane chart
   - redwood-data-plane chart
   - Any CRDs/operators required by upgrade hooks
2) Container images
   - Control plane + data plane images referenced by charts
   - Migration jobs and pre/ post-upgrade jobs images
3) Installer
   - redwood-private-installer binary
   - Plan schema version
4) Terraform module updates (as needed)
   - Version pinning variables
   - Upgrade window variables
   - Artifact sources (including mirrors) variables
5) Compatibility policy
   - Matrix / policy code that blocks unsupported upgrades (ex: N-2 -> N)
6) Audit log schema/events
   - Upgrade lifecycle events should be emitted in supported configurations
7) (On-prem) Offline upgrade bundle
   - Manifest
   - Checksums and signatures
   - Chart/image availability and mirror mapping


Version mapping rules (proposal)
We need a simple, enforceable mapping between “platform” and “tooling” so Support can say: “To upgrade to X, use installer Y+”.

Rule 1: Platform version is the primary version
- We speak in platform versions externally (ex: 2025.06.0-private).
- Everything else (installer/min terraform) is constrained relative to platform.

Rule 2: Each platform version declares minimum tooling versions
- The compatibility policy should specify:
  - min_installer_version
  - min_terraform_module_version (optional, only if required)
  - required_plan_schema_version
- Installer enforces this during plan generation (block early, do not start upgrade).

Rule 3: Tooling may be forward compatible within a bounded window
- Installer should support (platform N-1 and N) at minimum.
- Preferred: installer N can manage platform N-1 -> N upgrade.
- Non-goal: installer N supporting platform N-3.

Rule 4: Offline bundle is tied 1:1 to platform release
- Bundle version must match platform version exactly.
- Bundle contains chart versions and image digests pinned to the platform release.

Practical mapping table (working, for Q2)
- Platform 2025.05.x
  - min installer: 1.9.x (prechecks framework required)
  - min terraform: 0.14.x (version pinning + upgrade window)
- Platform 2025.06.x
  - min installer: 1.10.x (backup orchestrator + rollback command)
  - min terraform: 0.15.x (offline mirror endpoints)

Notes:
- The exact version numbers above are placeholders until we align with the actual tags from the PRs. Intention is what matters: platform declares mins; installer blocks if too old.


How we cut a Private release (step-by-step)
This is the “release captain” checklist. (Some of this is current; some is proposed standardization.)

0) Preconditions (must be true)
- No open Sev0/Sev1 incidents attributed to “upgrade/rollback mechanism” that are unresolved.
- Compatibility policy updated for the new platform version and reviewed by matrix owner (Quentin).
- Docs delta identified (even if not published yet). At minimum internal runbook updated.

1) Branch cut
- Cut release branch in:
  - redwood-helm-charts (charts)
  - redwood (platform, migrations, compatibility policy)
  - redwood-private-installer (only if tooling changes required for this platform)
  - redwood-terraform (only if new variables are required)
- Tag RC versions consistently:
  - charts: <platform>-rc.<n>
  - installer: <installer>-rc.<n>
  - terraform: <module>-rc.<n>

2) Build + publish candidate artifacts
- Publish charts to staging chart repo.
- Build + publish images to staging registry.
- Build installer RC binaries.
- Build offline upgrade bundle (on-prem lane) and publish to staging bucket.

3) Run required test matrix
- Must include N-1 -> N upgrade e2e.
- Must include rollback drill at least once per monthly stable cut (RC -> stable promotion requires it).
- Minimum environments:
  - VPC: EKS (current supported K8s minor), default storage backend
  - On-prem-ish: Kind/k3s + offline artifact mirror simulation OR lab cluster (if available)

4) Gate review
- Release Eng (Connor/Devon) reviews build provenance + artifact integrity.
- SRE (Sean/Rafael) reviews:
  - upgrade dashboards
  - migration duration distribution
  - error-rate deltas during upgrade window
  - rollback verification health
- Platform (Ethan/Michael) reviews:
  - migration guardrails
  - idempotency checks
  - compatibility policy correctness
- If a waiver is required, we must document:
  - what failed
  - customer impact (if any)
  - mitigation
  - explicit owner sign-off

5) Promote to stable
- Publish stable artifacts (production repos).
- Finalize release notes (internal) and “customer-facing delta” summary.
- Notify Support + Solutions with:
  - supported upgrade path(s)
  - minimum installer version
  - known issues
  - rollback notes (what is guaranteed vs best-effort)


Gating proposal (what blocks the release)
We need to codify gates so we can stop having “it seems fine” releases.

Gate A: Compatibility policy gate (blocking)
- Any platform release must include compatibility policy update.
- Policy must explicitly state supported upgrade paths (default: N-1 -> N).
- Installer must enforce the policy at plan generation time.

Gate B: Precheck suite health (blocking)
- Required prechecks must pass on reference clusters.
- If a precheck fails due to test environment limitations, we can waive with justification, but not for:
  - DB connectivity
  - RBAC/auth reachability
  - artifact availability
  - storage headroom below minimum

Gate C: Backup/restore hooks (blocking for stable; warning for RC)
- For monthly stable: at least one clean run where backup completes and restore verification steps are successful in the e2e.
- For weekly RC: backup hooks can be “warn-only” if rollback contract is not yet GA, but we should avoid shipping platform changes that are not recoverable.

Gate D: Rollback drill (blocking for stable)
- Stable promotion requires:
  - at least one rollback execution in an e2e environment
  - verification that core health checks pass post-rollback
  - confirmation that we preserve required audit trail of rollback invocation

Gate E: Artifact integrity (blocking)
- Offline bundle must verify checksums/signature.
- Image digests referenced in chart must exist in target registry/mirror.

Gate F: Observability + audit events (blocking for stable; warning for RC)
- Upgrade lifecycle audit events must be emitted (start, prechecks pass/fail, backup complete, rollback invoked, upgrade end).
- For stable, require field completeness for compliance: actor, target env/cluster id, versions (from/to), outcome.


Emergency lane (patch releases)
Definition: Sev0/S1 customer impact, security fix, or data-loss risk.
- Allowed to bypass some gates, but never bypass:
  - Artifact integrity (Gate E)
  - Compatibility policy gate (Gate A)
  - Minimum prechecks (DB connectivity + artifact availability + RBAC basic) subset of Gate B
- Must have explicit SRE on-call approval + Release Eng approval documented in the release ticket.
- Postmortem action required if we waived rollback drill or backup verification.


Notes from discussions (raw)
- SRE asked for a clear “recommend rollback vs fix forward” decision point in runbooks. Release train should include a default rollback recommendation when upgrade is in a failed/unknown state and data migrations are incomplete.
- On-prem constraints are still the biggest source of “unknown unknowns”: mirror endpoints, custom registries, and inconsistent DNS/TLS. We should treat bundle verification failures as blocking, not just noisy.
- CI timeouts: we’re seeing flakiness in upgrade e2e; if we accept retries, we must record retry count as part of evidence (to prevent masking real issues).


Open questions (need answers before GA)
1) What’s our official definition of “rollback guarantee”?
   - Restore to previous control plane/data plane versions? What about DB schema state? Are we guaranteeing schema rollback or only forward-compatible migrations + app rollback?
2) How do we represent upgrade plan + executed steps for auditability?
   - Where do we persist the plan artifact and state machine logs (support bundle vs cluster secret vs external store)?
3) Terraform version pinning: do we require a minimum terraform module version for every platform release, or only when the module changes?
4) Offline bundle signing: who holds keys, and what’s the customer verification flow?


Action items (Q2)
- [Connor] Draft formal “Private release gating policy” doc from these notes and get sign-off (SRE + Product). Target: 2025-05-15.
- [Sahana] Update CI evidence bundle: attach test matrix summary + links to logs to the release ticket. Target: 2025-05-22.
- [Quentin] Land compatibility policy enforcement in installer plan generation (block unsupported paths) and document N-1 rule. Target: aligns w/ platform PR.
- [Devon] Standardize version naming and tagging across repos (charts/installer/terraform). Target: 2025-06-01.
- [Elliot] Ensure docs delta is included in promotion checklist and that Support gets a “what changed” blurb each stable cut. Target: 2025-06-10.

Appendix: Evidence we want attached to each release ticket
- Git SHA + tag for each repo
- Chart versions and image digests
- Installer version + plan schema version
- Terraform module version (if relevant)
- Compatibility policy diff / matrix snapshot
- Test matrix results (upgrade + rollback)
- Audit event sample payloads from test run
- Waivers (if any) + approvals
